summary.one_liner: A long-form educational write-up explaining what happens step by step when you type a URL like google.com into a browser, from keypress through DNS, TLS, HTTP, server handling, and browser rendering.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a single narrative document, not a code project, that walks through the path of a web request. It covers keyboard input and autocomplete, URL parsing, the deprecated HSTS list, DNS resolution through browser, OS, router, and ISP caches, and recursive lookups. It then describes the TCP socket and TLS handshake, HTTP GET requests and responses (headers, cookies, caching, 301/304 codes), and server-side handling by httpd servers such as Apache or nginx. The final sections cover browser internals: HTML tokenizing and DOM construction, the render tree, CSS selector matching and specificity, layout, and painting. It ends with a short history of the web at CERN.
use_cases: Learning what happens when a URL is typed into a browser
Preparing for web fundamentals or system design interviews
Understanding DNS caching and TLS handshake steps
Understanding browser rendering pipeline: DOM, render tree, layout, paint
Explaining HTTP status codes and redirects to teammates
Reading background on why layout and reflow slow down pages
notable: Traces a full page load end to end, from keypress to pixels on screen
Covers DNS caching layers (browser, OS, router, ISP) and anycast or round-robin DNS
Explains the browser rendering pipeline: DOM tree, render tree, layout, and painting
Includes CSS selector specificity examples and why layout thrashing hurts performance
Lists browser engines (Blink, Gecko, WebKit) in a comparison table
caveats: Not a runnable project; it is documentation only
Some content is dated, such as the HSTS preload list (marked deprecated), SPDY (deprecated in favor of HTTP/2), and a 2010-era HTTP example
Parts of the text are informal opinion (e.g. comments on Angular and jQuery performance) and some sections are cut off or garbled in the source
keywords: what happens when you type a url
